purpose: Recorded debt ledger for migration-chain coherence. PR #881 recovered 88 migrations that the 2026-09-26 reset had deleted, and recovering a file is not the same as proving it is sound. This gate measures whether those migrations can rebuild the brain schema from empty. The migrations do not: core tables are used by them and created by none. This ledger records that debt BY NAME so it can never grow silently, and so every unrecorded finding fails the build.

floor_history.reason: Initial ledger recorded after PR #881 restored the migrations and proved a rebuild from empty is impossible. 11 core tables used by migrations, created by none.

Raised ONLY because three further uncreated tables appeared on main. The ledger was 11, the measurement became 14, and the original enforcement PRINTED the regression and then passed anyway, because its shell step ended with an unconditional `exit 0`. Run 36501228953 shows `floor=11 measured=14` on a successful job. The three added tables were introduced by the intelligence-commit migrations on main, each of which references a table nobody has ever created. The rise is recorded debt, not an accepted risk: see authority_note.

what_this_means: The migrations depend on 14 core tables that NO migration creates, including the canonical event store (nayanet_cognition_events) and v7_smart_note_transactions, which the chain contract names as the only legal source of Intelligent Block identity. These tables predate the migration history and were created directly in the live database: a search of the entire pre-reset history proves no migration ever created them, and no schema dump exists in any commit. Therefore master-plan item 26 (Rebuildability) and item 27 (Disaster Recovery) are NOT SATISFIED, and the brain schema cannot be reconstructed from source. This is a measured finding, not an opinion.
recoverability_of_the_definitions: NOT RECOVERABLE FROM SOURCE. The live database is the only holder of the true column names, types, constraints and policies. No migration, dump, or committed artefact in any branch of history defines these tables. Their shapes can only be inferred from usage (INSERT column lists, indexes, RLS policies, triggers), which establishes column NAMES but not authoritative TYPES. Authoring DDL from inferred types would be fabrication, so it has deliberately not been done.
how_to_lower_this_ledger: Author the missing CREATE TABLE migrations in dependency order, then re-run the gate and delete the repaired entries from known_defects. Repair must come from the live schema, not from inference. Never widen this ledger to make a build green: the ledger exists to make new debt visible, and a ledger that absorbs every change stops being a regression floor and becomes a rubber stamp. Control 5 in verify-migration-coherence-controls.py proves that supplying the missing CREATE statements drives the measurement to zero, so the findings are real and mechanically fixable rather than a hardcoded list.
authority_note: Authoring these migrations is real schema work against the canonical brain and belongs to whoever holds schema authority and live database access. This ledger records the defect; it does not decide or perform the repair.
